revision_of.reason: v1 had the correct computation-first direction but left too much ad hoc judgment in the formula, control, and exotic-input stages.

source_of_truth.normative_form: CTL revision payload admitted at claim:graph:computation-first-v1
source_of_truth.human_projection_policy: Human-readable org or diagrams may be generated later, but they are projections, not source of truth.
source_of_truth.payload_file_role: This JSON file is an admission preimage; after admission, the CTL object is normative.
source_of_truth.logical_id_note: The logical id keeps the v1 suffix for compatibility with the first admitted graph lane; graph_identity.version is the actual graph revision.

v1_assessment.verdict: directionally correct but too coarse for fast low-ad-hoc execution
kept: same dogfood store with split keys
problems_fixed: formula contract, implementation, and sanity checks were one large node
ordinary alpha=0 controls were not a separate gate
presentation invariance had too little structure
exotic input discovery started too late
artifact schema and exact certificate requirements were implicit
equal exotic values did not specify the next fast path

split_policy.store_strategy: same project-local ctl-dogfood store for now
split_policy.future_split_rule: If graph volume or governance diverges, move objects whose graph_id or portable_split_key matches this graph into a graph-specific store and preserve original CIDs as external references.

scope.primary_goal: Compute twisted Yetter examples correctly and quickly, then evaluate known exotic pairs with enough confidence that equal or different values are meaningful.
scope.first_formula_scope: minimal exact Kirby-matrix / omega-theta computation for small closed examples, with any unproved closed-manifold assumptions explicitly marked
excluded_for_v2: full decorated Reutter no-go program before computations

minimum_exotic_entry_gate: formula contract accepted or explicitly labeled experimental
at least one nontrivial presentation-invariance gate passes
exotic input has auditable marking level

subagent_ready_when: node can output artifact paths or a CTL claim
execution_policy.recording_rule: Each completed node appends a CTL claim or lab-note object with commands, outputs, exact artifacts, status, and next edge.
execution_policy.routing_rule: When a node fails by a listed failure condition, follow the matching edge instead of re-planning from scratch.
execution_policy.anti_overthinking_rule: Do not begin no-go analysis merely because a first small example is boring; compute more examples or another category unless a gate says the formula is not meaningful.

acceptance: uv run python -m pytest is the default test command
exact arithmetic dependency choice is recorded
generated caches are ignored
CTL provider pin remains unchanged
failure_conditions: dependency cannot be installed without changing research scope

list of normalization, signature, orientation, and handle assumptions

nodes.goal: Classify the exotic computation without overclaiming.

same values route to next target or category, not immediate no-go
inconclusive values route to the earliest blocking node

nodes.goal: Choose the fastest next computation when the first exotic pair does not distinguish.

if multiple exotic pairs agree, consider another small category before no-go

failure_conditions: current category is provably uninformative for the tested scope
all next steps require theory work

nodes.goal: Record systematic negative evidence after many correct computations agree.

tested categories, pairs, and markings are explicit

nodes.goal: Record that computation is blocked by a mathematical ambiguity or likely no-go issue.
